Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:176884
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 16921 of 2024

Applicant :- Rajaram Yadav
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sudhir Kumar Tripathi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Sudhir Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar,
learned Aga for the State.

2.  The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.783 of 2020, under Sections 376, 506, 313 IPC, Police Station GIDA, District Gorakhpur, during pendency of the trial.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first bail application of the applicant was dismissed on 11.10.2023 by this Bench after considering the fact that applicant tried to evade his arrest and did not even comply the earlier order passed by this Court and he is pressing the instant second bail application on the ground that in the present matter, he is in jail since 11.08.2023 i.e. for last more than a year.
4.

He further submits that as far as merit of the present case is concerned, admittedly, victim is major and married lady and FIR of the present case was lodged after 3 months and she appears to Rajaram Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18805762/
1 be consenting party and, therefore, considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant should be released on bail.

entities.text: Rajaram Yadav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He next submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history.

5. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submits that this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant but could not dispute the fact that first bail application of the applicant was dismissed on the ground that despite repeated orders passed by this Court,
applicant failed to appear before the court concerned within stipulated time and in the present matter, applicant is in jail for last more than a year.
6.
Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that victim is a major and married lady and she appears to be consenting party and FIR of the present case was lodged after 3 months.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. However, this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first bail application of the applicant was dismissed vide order dated 11.10.2023 but it appears that his first bail application was dismissed on the ground that in spite of repeated orders passed by this Court applicant did not appear before the Court concerned but in the present matter, he is in jail since August, 2023 i.e. for last more than a year.

9. As far as merit of the present case is concerned, it reflects that FIR of the present case was lodged after 3 months and informant i.e. victim of the case is major and married lady and she appears to be consenting party.
Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history.

10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Rajaram Yadav be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
